units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 26a:13">R. Hash. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>אין קטיגור נעשה ס׳</he> the accuser (gold reminding of the golden calf) must not be made an advocate (therefore must the high priest on the Day of Atonement not enter the Holy of Holies in gold-embroidered garments); <cite ref="Berakhot 59a:2">Ber. 59ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Chagigah 13b:6">Ḥag. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>קטיגור יעשה ס׳</he> shall the accuser (the ox or calf) become an advocate? <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 30:6">Lev. R. s. 30</cite> <he>אוי … סְנֵיגוֹרוֹ וכ׳</he> woe to this man, his advocate has turned prosecutor!; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 3:1:2">Y. Succ. III, beg. 53ᶜ</cite> <he>שניגורו</he> (corr. acc.); a. fr.—Pl. <he>סְנֵיגוֹרִים</he>, <he>סְנֵיגוֹרִין</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:3:5">Y. R. Hash. I, 57ᵇ</cite> top; a. fr.—Mekh. Mishp., s. 20 (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 23:7">Ex. XXIII, 7</cite>) <he>שלא יעמיד אצלו ס׳ וכ׳</he> that he (the judge) must not allow advocates to stand by his side (in place of the parties themselves), for it is said, ‘before the judge the words of both of them must come’ (ib. XXII, 8); [<cite ref="Shevuot 30b:13">Shebu. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>שלא יעשה סניגרון לדבריו</he> (Ms. M. <he>יעשה דבריו סנגרון</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 352:11">Yalk. Ex. 352</cite> <he>שלא יעשה סניגורין לדבריו</he>) that he must not appoint advocates for what he has to say (in defense of his decision, if a point of law is raised against it); the entire passage seems to require emendation in accordance with Mekh. l. c.]
